q: How tall is the Eiffel Tower, including its antennas?
hint: For scale: a 30-storey office tower is about {100 m} tall.
card: Its iron expands in summer heat, so the tower grows by up to about 15 cm.

q: How tall is the Burj Khalifa in Dubai?
hint: For scale: the Empire State Building’s roof is {381 m} up.
card: It has been the tallest building in the world since it opened in 2010.

q: In what year did the Golden Gate Bridge open?
hint: For scale: Ford’s Model T went on sale in 1908.
card: Its official paint colour is called International Orange.

q: How tall is the Elizabeth Tower, home of Big Ben?
hint: For scale: an Olympic swimming pool is {50 m} long.
card: Big Ben is the bell inside. The tower was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012.

q: How tall was the Great Pyramid of Giza when it was finished?
hint: For scale: a football pitch is about {100 m} long.
card: It stayed the tallest human-made structure for more than 3,800 years.

q: In what year did the Panama Canal open?
hint: For scale: the Suez Canal opened in 1869.
card: Locks lift each ship about 26 metres up to Gatun Lake and back down again.

q: How tall is the Statue of Liberty, from the ground to the tip of the torch?
hint: For scale: a two-storey house is about {8 m} tall.
card: Her copper skin is only about 2.4 mm thick, roughly two coins stacked.

q: How long is the main span of the Golden Gate Bridge?
hint: For scale: a big airport runway is about {3,000 m} long.
card: It was the longest suspension span in the world when it opened.

q: In what year AD was the Colosseum in Rome completed?
hint: For scale: Julius Caesar died in 44 BC.
card: It held an estimated 50,000 or more spectators.

q: How many floors does the Empire State Building have?
hint: For scale: the Burj Khalifa has 163 floors.
card: Construction took just over a year, finishing in 1931.

q: What is the average distance from Earth to the Moon?
hint: For scale: Earth is about {12,700 km} across.
card: Light makes the trip in about 1.3 seconds.

q: How many Earth days does Mars take to orbit the Sun once?
hint: For scale: Earth takes 365 days to go round the Sun.
card: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.

q: Roughly how high above Earth does the International Space Station orbit?
hint: For scale: airliners cruise at about {11 km}.
card: It circles the whole planet roughly every 90 minutes.

q: How fast does light travel in a vacuum?
hint: For scale: sound moves at about {0.34 km/s}.
card: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth.

q: In what year did Apollo 11 land on the Moon?
hint: For scale: the first person reached space in 1961.
card: Armstrong and Aldrin spent about two and a half hours walking on the surface.

q: In what year was Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, launched?
hint: For scale: World War II ended in 1945.
card: It was a polished sphere just 58 cm across.

q: Roughly how hot is the visible surface of the Sun?
hint: For scale: lava erupts at about {1,200 °C}.
card: The core is far hotter, at around 15 million °C.

q: In what year was the Hubble Space Telescope launched?
hint: For scale: the Space Shuttle first flew in 1981.
card: It orbits roughly 500 km up, above the blur of the atmosphere.

q: From what height did Felix Baumgartner make his record 2012 skydive?
hint: For scale: airliners cruise at about {11 km}.
card: He broke the speed of sound in free fall. You pass his height on the way up.

q: In what year did people first fly in a hot-air balloon?
hint: For scale: Isaac Newton died in 1727.
card: A few weeks earlier, the first passengers had been a sheep, a duck and a rooster.

q: How tall is Mount Everest above sea level?
hint: For scale: Mont Blanc, the highest Alp, is {4,808 m}.
card: That figure comes from a joint China–Nepal survey announced in 2020.

q: What is the diameter of the Earth?
hint: For scale: New York to London is about {5,570 km}.
card: Earth is slightly wider at the equator than it is from pole to pole.

q: How many bones are in an adult human body?
hint: For scale: your spine alone has 33 vertebrae.
card: Babies start with around 300. Many fuse together as they grow.

q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
hint: For scale: humans have one heart with four chambers.
card: Its blood is blue, thanks to a copper-based protein.

q: How long can a blue whale grow?
hint: For scale: a school bus is about {12 m} long.
card: It is the largest animal known to have ever lived.

q: How many teeth does a full adult human set have, wisdom teeth included?
hint: For scale: children have 20 baby teeth.
card: Four of those are wisdom teeth, and many people never get all four.

q: Roughly how many times does a human heart beat in one day?
hint: For scale: a day has 1,440 minutes.
card: Over an average lifetime that adds up to roughly 2.5 billion beats.

q: How many bones are in one human hand, wrist included?
hint: For scale: each finger has three bones; the thumb has two.
card: Your two hands hold about a quarter of all the bones in your body.

q: How long is an African elephant pregnant?
hint: For scale: a human pregnancy lasts about 9 months.
card: It is the longest pregnancy of any land mammal.

q: How many vertebrae are in a giraffe’s neck?
hint: For scale: a giraffe’s neck can be {1.8 m} long.
card: The same number as yours. Each one is just much longer.

q: How tall is Hyperion, the tallest known living tree?
hint: For scale: a 30-storey building is about {100 m} tall.
card: Its exact location in California is kept secret to protect it.

q: How long does a human red blood cell live?
hint: For scale: skin cells are replaced every 2 to 4 weeks.
card: Your body makes millions of new ones every second.

q: In what year did the Titanic sink?
hint: For scale: Queen Victoria died in 1901.
card: It went down less than three hours after hitting the iceberg, on its maiden voyage.

q: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall?
hint: For scale: the Wall went up in 1961.
card: It had divided the city for 28 years.

q: In what year did Columbus first reach the Americas?
hint: For scale: Gutenberg printed his Bible around 1455.
card: He was trying to reach Asia by sailing west.

q: In what year was William Shakespeare born?
hint: For scale: Elizabeth I became queen in 1558.
card: Galileo was born the same year.

q: In what year did the Wright brothers make the first powered flight?
hint: For scale: the first cars went on sale in the 1890s.
card: The first flight lasted 12 seconds and covered 37 metres.

q: In what year were the first modern Olympic Games held?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower opened in 1889.
card: They were held in Athens.

q: In what year was the Magna Carta sealed?
hint: For scale: the Norman conquest of England was in 1066.
card: Only four original copies from that year survive.

q: In what year was the US Declaration of Independence adopted?
hint: For scale: the French Revolution began in 1789.
card: Most delegates signed the famous copy on August 2, not July 4.

q: In what year AD did the Western Roman Empire fall?
hint: For scale: Constantinople was founded in 330.
card: Its last emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was a teenager.

q: In what year was Coca-Cola first sold?
hint: For scale: the telephone was patented in 1876.
card: It was first served at a pharmacy soda fountain in Atlanta.

q: In what year was the first iPhone released?
hint: For scale: YouTube launched in 2005.
card: It launched without an App Store. That arrived a year later.

q: In what year did Concorde begin carrying passengers?
hint: For scale: the Boeing 747 entered service in 1970.
card: It crossed the Atlantic in about three and a half hours.

q: At about what altitude did Concorde cruise?
hint: For scale: airliners cruise at about {11 km}.
card: Passengers could see the curve of the Earth from their seats.

q: How fast does sound travel through air at 20 °C?
hint: For scale: a cruising airliner does about {250 m/s}.
card: In water, sound travels more than four times faster.

q: In what year was the Rubik’s Cube invented?
hint: For scale: pocket calculators appeared around 1970.
card: It has about 43 quintillion possible positions.

q: How many keys does a standard piano have?
hint: For scale: a guitar has 6 strings and about 20 frets.
card: 52 of them are white and 36 are black.

q: In what year did Ford start selling the Model T?
hint: For scale: Karl Benz built his first car in 1885.
card: From 1913 its moving assembly line cut build time from over 12 hours to about 90 minutes.

q: In what year did the World Wide Web become publicly available?
hint: For scale: the first Macintosh went on sale in 1984.
card: The first website, at CERN, has been restored and is still online.

q: How many seconds are in one day?
hint: For scale: an hour has 3,600 seconds.
card: Earth’s spin wobbles slightly, which is why leap seconds were invented.

q: How long is a marathon?
hint: For scale: a 10K race is {10 km}.
card: The odd distance was fixed at the 1908 London Olympics.

q: How many different first moves can White make in chess?
hint: For scale: each side starts with 16 pieces.
card: Sixteen pawn moves plus four knight moves.

q: How many member states does the United Nations have?
hint: For scale: the European Union has 27 members.
card: South Sudan was the most recent to join, in 2011.

q: How many time zones does Russia span?
hint: For scale: the mainland USA spans 4 time zones.
card: When it is 9 a.m. in Moscow, it is 6 p.m. in Kamchatka.

q: How many elements are on the periodic table?
hint: For scale: about 92 elements occur naturally on Earth.
card: The four newest names were made official in 2016.

q: How many hours are in a week?
hint: For scale: a full-time work week is about 40 hours.
card: If you sleep eight hours a night, 56 of them are spent asleep.

q: Roughly how long is the River Nile?
hint: For scale: the USA is about {4,500 km} wide.
card: It flows north and passes through 11 countries.

q: How deep is the Challenger Deep, the lowest known point of the ocean?
hint: For scale: the average ocean is about {3,700 m} deep.
card: Mount Everest would fit inside it with about 2 km of water to spare.

q: How many countries are in Africa?
hint: For scale: Europe has about 44 countries.
card: Nigeria has the largest population of them.

q: How tall is the Leaning Tower of Pisa?
hint: For scale: a 10-storey building is about {30 m} tall.
card: It leans about 4 degrees, down from 5.5 before engineers steadied it in 2001.

q: In what year did the Sydney Opera House open?
hint: For scale: the Beatles split up in 1970.
card: Its architect, Jørn Utzon, left the project in 1966 and never saw it finished.

q: How long is the Great Wall of China, counting every branch?
hint: For scale: the Earth is about {40,075 km} around the equator.
card: The figure comes from a 2012 Chinese survey that measured every wall, trench and branch.

q: How tall is the Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio, not counting its pedestal?
hint: For scale: a giraffe is about {5.5 m} tall.
card: Its outstretched arms span 28 metres, almost as wide as it is tall.

q: In what year was the Eiffel Tower completed?
hint: For scale: Thomas Edison demonstrated his light bulb in 1879.
card: It was built as the entrance arch for a World’s Fair and was meant to stand for only 20 years.

q: How long is the Channel Tunnel between England and France?
hint: For scale: a marathon is about {42 km}.
card: About 38 km of it runs under the seabed, the longest undersea stretch of any tunnel.

q: How tall are the Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is about {330 m} tall.
card: From 1998 to 2004 they were the tallest buildings in the world.

q: In what year did the Brooklyn Bridge open?
hint: For scale: the US Civil War ended in 1865.
card: Its main span was the longest suspension span in the world when it opened.

q: How tall is the Hoover Dam?
hint: For scale: the Statue of Liberty, ground to torch, is about {93 m}.
card: Its concrete was cooled with chilled-water pipes; left alone it would have taken over a century to cool.

q: In what year did the Empire State Building open?
hint: For scale: the Wall Street Crash happened in 1929.
card: It went up in about 13 months, at times rising more than four floors a week.

q: How long is the Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge in China, the world’s longest bridge?
hint: For scale: a marathon is about {42 km}.
card: It carries the Beijing–Shanghai high-speed railway, much of it over rice paddies and lakes.

q: How many seconds does sunlight take to reach Earth?
hint: For scale: moonlight reaches us in about 1.3 seconds.
card: So you always see the Sun as it was a little over eight minutes ago.

q: What is the diameter of the Moon?
hint: For scale: the USA is about {4,500 km} wide.
card: The Moon is drifting away from Earth by about 3.8 cm a year.

q: Roughly how hot is the surface of Venus?
hint: For scale: lead melts at {327 °C}.
card: Venus is hotter than Mercury, even though it is nearly twice as far from the Sun.

q: In what year did Yuri Gagarin become the first person in space?
hint: For scale: the Korean War ended in 1953.
card: His flight, Vostok 1, lasted 108 minutes and circled Earth once.

q: How many Earth days long is a year on Mercury?
hint: For scale: an Earth month is about 30 days.
card: Yet one Mercury day, sunrise to sunrise, lasts about 176 Earth days.

q: What speed must something reach to escape Earth’s gravity from the surface?
hint: For scale: a rifle bullet flies at about {1 km/s}.
card: That is about 40,000 km/h. Staying in low orbit takes a little less, about 7.8 km/s.

q: In what year was Voyager 1 launched?
hint: For scale: the first Space Shuttle flew in 1981.
card: It is now the most distant human-made object, more than 20 billion km away.

q: How many hours long is a day on Jupiter?
hint: For scale: an Earth day is 24 hours.
card: It is the fastest-spinning planet, which visibly squashes it at the poles.

q: How many Earths would fit side by side across the Sun?
hint: For scale: Jupiter is about 11 Earths across.
card: By volume, the Sun could hold about 1.3 million Earths.

q: What is the average distance from the Earth to the Sun?
hint: For scale: Jupiter is about five times farther from the Sun than we are.
card: This distance is one astronomical unit, the yardstick of the solar system.

q: In what year was Pluto reclassified as a dwarf planet?
hint: For scale: the euro became cash in 2002.
card: The vote was taken at the International Astronomical Union’s meeting in Prague.

q: How many people have walked on the Moon?
hint: For scale: NASA flew nine crewed missions to the Moon.
card: All of them walked there between 1969 and 1972; no one has been back since.

q: How many legs does a lobster have?
hint: For scale: insects have six legs.
card: Lobsters taste and smell with tiny hairs on their legs.

q: Roughly how much does an adult male African elephant weigh?
hint: For scale: a family car weighs about {1,500 kg}.
card: Despite that bulk, elephants walk almost silently on padded feet.

q: How many eyes does a honeybee have?
hint: For scale: most spiders have eight.
card: The three small ones on top of its head sense light and help it hold a level flight.

q: How many chambers does a cow’s stomach have?
hint: For scale: a human stomach has just one.
card: The largest, the rumen, can hold well over 100 litres of chewed grass.

q: Up to how many times a minute can a hummingbird’s heart beat?
hint: For scale: a resting human heart beats about 70 times a minute.
card: At night some hummingbirds drop into torpor, slowing it to under 100.

q: For how many minutes can a sperm whale hold its breath on a dive?
hint: For scale: most people can manage about one minute.
card: They dive past 1,000 metres to hunt squid in total darkness.

q: How tall can an ostrich grow?
hint: For scale: a typical doorway is about {2 m} tall.
card: An ostrich’s eye is bigger than its brain.

q: What is the widest wingspan of a wandering albatross?
hint: For scale: an average man is about {1.75 m} tall.
card: It can glide for hours without flapping, covering thousands of kilometres a week.

q: Roughly how many neurons are in the human brain?
hint: For scale: a honeybee’s brain has about a million.
card: They link up through something like 100 trillion connections.

q: How many teeth does an adult dog have?
hint: For scale: an adult cat has 30.
card: Puppies have 28 baby teeth and lose them by about six months old.

q: How fast can a peregrine falcon dive?
hint: For scale: a Formula 1 car tops out around {350 km/h}.
card: That makes it the fastest animal on Earth.

q: Roughly what percentage of an adult human body is water?
hint: For scale: about 71% of Earth’s surface is ocean.
card: The brain and heart are closer to three-quarters water.

q: In what year did the Great Fire of London happen?
hint: For scale: Shakespeare died in 1616.
card: It destroyed over 13,000 houses, yet only a handful of deaths were recorded.

q: In what year did American women win the right to vote nationwide?
hint: For scale: the First World War ended in 1918.
card: New Zealand had given women the vote back in 1893, the first self-governing country to do so.

q: In what year was the Battle of Hastings fought?
hint: For scale: Vikings first raided Lindisfarne in 793.
card: Its story is stitched into the Bayeux Tapestry, which is about 70 metres long.

q: In what year was Napoleon defeated at Waterloo?
hint: For scale: the French Revolution began in 1789.
card: The battlefield lies in today’s Belgium, about 15 km south of Brussels.

q: In what year did the Black Death reach Europe?
hint: For scale: Marco Polo set off for China in 1271.
card: It killed perhaps a third to a half of Europe’s population within a few years.

q: In what year did Martin Luther publish his Ninety-five Theses?
hint: For scale: the Ottomans captured Constantinople in 1453.
card: Printing presses spread his ideas across Germany within weeks.

q: In what year did the Chernobyl nuclear disaster happen?
hint: For scale: the Live Aid concerts were held in 1985.
card: The exclusion zone around it still covers about 2,600 square kilometres.

q: In what year did the Mayflower reach America?
hint: For scale: Shakespeare died in 1616.
card: About 100 passengers made the crossing, which took 66 days.

q: In what year was the Boston Tea Party?
hint: For scale: George Washington was born in 1732.
card: About 340 chests of tea were dumped into Boston Harbor.

q: In what year did India gain independence?
hint: For scale: the Second World War ended in 1945.
card: Independence Day is celebrated every year on 15 August.

q: In what year was the first email sent between two computers?
hint: For scale: the first video game console went on sale in 1972.
card: Ray Tomlinson chose the @ sign to separate the user from the computer’s name.

q: In what year was the Statue of Liberty dedicated?
hint: For scale: Thomas Edison demonstrated his light bulb in 1879.
card: It was a gift from France; its copper skin is only about 2.4 mm thick.

q: In what year did the first jet airliner enter passenger service?
hint: For scale: the Second World War ended in 1945.
card: It was the de Havilland Comet, which cut flight times almost in half.

q: What is the wingspan of an Airbus A380?
hint: For scale: a Boeing 737 spans about {36 m}.
card: Its wings cover about 845 square metres, roughly two basketball courts.

q: How many transistors are on Apple’s M1 chip?
hint: For scale: the first microprocessor, in 1971, had about 2,300.
card: Each one is just a few nanometres across, far smaller than a virus.

q: What is the rail speed record, set by a French TGV in 2007?
hint: For scale: a Formula 1 car tops out around {350 km/h}.
card: The record run used a specially shortened train with bigger wheels and boosted voltage.

q: How many engines powered the first stage of the Saturn V moon rocket?
hint: For scale: SpaceX’s Super Heavy booster has 33.
card: Together they burned more than 12 tonnes of propellant every second.

q: In what year was the first call made from a handheld mobile phone?
hint: For scale: the Watergate scandal broke in 1972.
card: Martin Cooper of Motorola made the call on a New York street, to a rival at Bell Labs.

q: How many seconds did the Wright brothers’ first powered flight last?
hint: For scale: it covered about {37 m}.
card: The whole flight was shorter than the wingspan of a Boeing 747.

q: How many pixels does a 4K Ultra HD screen have?
hint: For scale: a Full HD screen is 1,920 by 1,080 pixels.
card: The name comes from its width of roughly 4,000 pixels.

q: What top speed did the X-15 rocket plane reach, the fastest crewed aircraft?
hint: For scale: Concorde cruised at about {2,180 km/h}.
card: It flew so high that some of its pilots earned astronaut wings.

q: In what year did the Boeing 747 begin carrying passengers?
hint: For scale: Concorde first flew in 1969.
card: It more than doubled passenger capacity and earned the nickname Jumbo Jet.

q: In what year was a barcode first scanned at a store checkout?
hint: For scale: the first Apple computer went on sale in 1976.
card: The first item scanned was a pack of Wrigley’s chewing gum.

q: How many squares make up the grid of a chessboard?
hint: For scale: a tic-tac-toe grid has nine.
card: Every board is set with a light square in each player’s right-hand corner.

q: What is the area of Australia?
hint: For scale: France is about 550,000 square km.
card: It is the only country that covers an entire continent.

q: Roughly how many languages are spoken in the world today?
hint: For scale: the European Union has 24 official languages.
card: About 40% of them are endangered, many with fewer than 1,000 speakers.

q: How deep is Lake Baikal, the world’s deepest lake?
hint: For scale: the Empire State Building’s roof is {381 m} up.
card: It holds roughly a fifth of the world’s unfrozen fresh surface water.

q: How tall is Angel Falls in Venezuela, the world’s highest waterfall?
hint: For scale: Niagara Falls drops about {51 m}.
card: Much of the water turns to mist before it reaches the bottom.

q: Roughly how many islands make up Indonesia?
hint: For scale: the Philippines has more than 7,000.
card: Only about 6,000 of them are inhabited.

q: Roughly how large is the Sahara Desert?
hint: For scale: France is about 550,000 square km.
card: Sand dunes cover only about a quarter of it; most of it is rocky plateau.

q: How many dots are there on a standard six-sided die?
hint: For scale: opposite faces of a die always add up to seven.
card: That same rule means the 1, 2 and 3 faces always meet at one corner.

q: How tall is Mount Kilimanjaro?
hint: For scale: Mount Everest is {8,849 m} tall.
card: Despite sitting near the equator, its summit still has glaciers.

q: Roughly how many litres of air does an adult breathe in a day?
hint: For scale: one relaxed breath is about half a litre.
card: That is enough to fill about 50 bathtubs.

q: How many minutes are in a week?
hint: For scale: an hour has 60 minutes.
card: That is seven days of 1,440 minutes each.

q: How fast does sound travel through water?
hint: For scale: a jet airliner cruises at about {250 m/s}.
card: That is why whales can hear one another across huge distances.

q: How tall is the Shard in London?
hint: For scale: a 10-storey building is about {30 m} tall.
card: When it opened in 2012 it was the tallest building in the European Union.

q: How tall is the Taj Mahal, from the ground to the tip of its dome?
hint: For scale: a giraffe stands about {5.5 m} tall.
card: Its four minarets were built leaning slightly outwards, so in an earthquake they would fall away from the tomb.

q: How tall is the Space Needle in Seattle?
hint: For scale: the Statue of Liberty reaches {93 m} to the tip of its torch.
card: It was built for the 1962 World’s Fair in less than a year.

q: How tall is the CN Tower in Toronto?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is {330 m} tall with its antennas.
card: It was the world’s tallest free-standing structure for over 30 years.

q: In what year did the Sydney Harbour Bridge open?
hint: For scale: the Titanic sank in 1912.
card: Sydneysiders nicknamed it “the Coathanger” for the shape of its arch.

q: How tall is each president’s head carved into Mount Rushmore?
hint: For scale: a giraffe stands about {5.5 m} tall.
card: Workers carved it between 1927 and 1941, and not one of them died on the job.

q: How long is the Panama Canal, from ocean to ocean?
hint: For scale: a marathon is just over {42 km}.
card: Locks lift ships about 26 m to cross Gatun Lake, then lower them back down to the sea.

q: How tall is the Arc de Triomphe in Paris?
hint: For scale: a 10-storey building is about {30 m} tall.
card: In 1919, three weeks after the First World War victory parade, a pilot flew a biplane through its arch.

q: How tall is the Gateway Arch in St. Louis?
hint: For scale: a football pitch is about {105 m} long.
card: It is exactly as wide between its legs as it is tall.

q: How tall is the Tokyo Skytree?
hint: For scale: the Empire State Building’s roof is {381 m} up.
card: Its official colour, “Skytree White”, is based on aijiro, a traditional Japanese pale blue-white.

q: How tall is the Washington Monument?
hint: For scale: a 30-storey office tower is about {100 m} tall.
card: Its stone changes shade partway up, where building paused for over 20 years.

q: In what year did the London Underground’s first line open?
hint: For scale: the world’s first public steam railway opened in 1825.
card: Its first trains were pulled by steam engines through shallow tunnels dug from the street.

q: How many moons does Mars have?
hint: For scale: Earth has one.
card: They are called Phobos and Deimos, Greek for “fear” and “dread”.

q: How much did Sputnik 1, the first satellite, weigh?
hint: For scale: a grand piano weighs about {300 kg}.
card: It sent out simple radio beeps that amateur radio operators around the world could pick up.

q: How many Earth years does Saturn take to orbit the Sun?
hint: For scale: Jupiter takes about 12 years.
card: Saturn is less dense than water, so in a big enough bathtub it would float.

q: How many Earth days does Venus take to spin once on its axis?
hint: For scale: Earth spins once a day, and Mars takes only slightly longer.
card: That’s longer than its year: Venus goes round the Sun in about 225 Earth days.

q: How many Earths could fit inside Jupiter?
hint: For scale: about 49 Moons would fit inside Earth.
card: Jupiter has more than twice the mass of all the other planets put together.

q: In what year did Halley’s Comet last pass close to Earth?
hint: For scale: Voyager 1 was launched in 1977.
card: It comes back about every 76 years, so its next visit is due in 2061.

q: How far does light travel in one year?
hint: For scale: the Sun is about {150,000,000 km} from Earth.
card: The nearest star beyond the Sun, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.2 light-years away.

q: How far is Mars from the Sun, on average?
hint: For scale: Earth orbits about {150,000,000 km} from the Sun.
card: Its red colour comes from iron oxide, essentially rust, in its dust.

q: How many of the Solar System’s planets have rings?
hint: For scale: the Solar System has eight planets.
card: Saturn’s are by far the brightest; the rings of Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune are faint and dark.

q: In what year did a Space Shuttle first fly into space?
hint: For scale: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon in 1969.
card: The first orbiter to reach space, Columbia, flew with just two astronauts on board.

q: How fast does the International Space Station travel?
hint: For scale: a passenger jet cruises at about {900 km/h}.
card: Its crew sees about 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets every day.

q: How many days did the whole Apollo 11 mission last, launch to splashdown?
hint: For scale: the trip from Earth to the Moon takes about three days.
card: Armstrong and Aldrin spent about 21 hours on the Moon, but only about 2.5 hours walking outside.

q: How many teeth does an adult cat have?
hint: For scale: an adult dog has 42.
card: Kittens start out with 26 smaller milk teeth.

q: How many chromosomes are in a typical human body cell?
hint: For scale: a fruit fly has 8.
card: A potato has 48, two more than we do.

q: How many bones make up the adult human skull?
hint: For scale: one hand and wrist contain 27 bones.
card: Only one of them, the lower jaw, can move freely.

q: How many ribs does a typical adult human have?
hint: For scale: the neck has seven vertebrae.
card: The lowest two pairs are called “floating ribs” because they don’t attach to the breastbone.

q: How many milk teeth does a child have in a full set?
hint: For scale: a full adult set has 32.
card: They start forming before birth, and the first usually appears at around six months old.

q: How much does an ostrich egg weigh?
hint: For scale: a large chicken egg weighs about {0.06 kg}.
card: It is the largest egg of any living bird, yet the smallest compared with the size of the bird.

q: How many days does a chicken egg take to hatch?
hint: For scale: a human pregnancy lasts about 40 weeks.
card: A chick uses a tiny spike on its beak, the egg tooth, to break out of the shell.

q: How tall is General Sherman, the giant sequoia in California?
hint: For scale: a blue whale can grow to about {30 m} long.
card: By volume it is the largest known single-stem tree on Earth.

q: Roughly how many hairs grow on a typical human head?
hint: For scale: a single hair grows about 1 cm a month.
card: Blondes tend to have the most hairs on their heads, and redheads the fewest.

q: In what year was Dolly the sheep, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, born?
hint: For scale: the World Wide Web went public in 1991.
card: She was named after the singer Dolly Parton.

q: In what year did Charles Darwin publish On the Origin of Species?
hint: For scale: Abraham Lincoln became US president in 1861.
card: Booksellers snapped up the first print run of 1,250 copies before it was even published.

q: Roughly how many quills does a North American porcupine have?
hint: For scale: a hedgehog has around 5,000 spines.
card: Porcupines can’t shoot their quills; they come loose when something touches them.

q: How many years did the Hundred Years’ War between England and France actually last?
hint: For scale: a human lifetime is about 80 years.
card: It ran from 1337 to 1453, though not continuously: long truces broke up the fighting.

q: How many people signed the US Declaration of Independence?
hint: For scale: the US Senate has 100 members.
card: John Hancock signed so large that “John Hancock” became American slang for a signature.

q: For how many years did Queen Victoria reign?
hint: For scale: a typical working life is about 40 years.
card: Her record as Britain’s longest-reigning monarch stood until Elizabeth II passed it in 2015.

q: In what year did people first reach the South Pole?
hint: For scale: Queen Victoria died in 1901.
card: Roald Amundsen’s Norwegian team beat Robert Falcon Scott’s British team there by about five weeks.

q: In what year was the first Harry Potter book published?
hint: For scale: the first Toy Story film came out in 1995.
card: Its first UK print run was just 500 copies.

q: In what year did Mickey Mouse first appear on screen in Steamboat Willie?
hint: For scale: the Empire State Building opened in 1931.
card: It was one of the first cartoons with fully synchronised sound, and Walt Disney voiced Mickey himself.

q: In what year was the first Star Wars film released?
hint: For scale: Jaws, often called the first summer blockbuster, came out in 1975.
card: Darth Vader’s voice was dubbed by James Earl Jones, who at first went uncredited.

q: In what year did the United States buy Alaska from Russia?
hint: For scale: the American Civil War ended in 1865.
card: The price worked out at about two cents per acre.

q: In what year was the first FIFA World Cup played?
hint: For scale: the first modern Olympics were held in 1896.
card: Uruguay hosted and won it, beating Argentina 4–2 in the final.

q: In what year was Tutankhamun’s tomb discovered?
hint: For scale: the First World War ended in 1918.
card: Howard Carter’s team spent about ten years cataloguing the more than 5,000 objects inside.

q: In what year were the first Nobel Prizes awarded?
hint: For scale: Alfred Nobel died in 1896.
card: Wilhelm Röntgen won the first physics prize, for discovering X-rays.

q: In what year did euro notes and coins first go into circulation?
hint: For scale: the euro first existed as an electronic currency in 1999.
card: Twelve countries switched their cash at once, the biggest currency changeover in history.

q: In what year did Charles Lindbergh fly solo nonstop across the Atlantic?
hint: For scale: the Wright brothers first flew in 1903.
card: The flight from New York to Paris took about 33.5 hours, with no co-pilot to take over.

q: What is the most passengers an Airbus A380 is certified to carry?
hint: For scale: a Boeing 737 seats about 160 to 190.
card: Its upper deck runs the full length of the plane, making it the largest passenger airliner ever built.

q: How many strings does a modern concert harp have?
hint: For scale: a standard guitar has six.
card: Its red strings mark every C and its black or blue strings every F, so harpists can find their place.

q: In what year did Nintendo release the first Game Boy?
hint: For scale: the Rubik’s Cube was invented in 1974.
card: Bundled with Tetris outside Japan, it and the Game Boy Color sold over 118 million units.

q: In what year did Alexander Graham Bell patent the telephone?
hint: For scale: the first transatlantic telegraph cable carried messages in 1858.
card: His first words over it were “Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.”

q: How tall was the Saturn V moon rocket?
hint: For scale: the Statue of Liberty reaches {93 m} to the tip of its torch.
card: It carried 24 astronauts toward the Moon over nine crewed missions.

q: How many wheels are on a Boeing 747’s landing gear?
hint: For scale: a typical car has four.
card: Sixteen sit on four main gear legs, two under the wings and two under the body, plus two on the nose gear.

q: How many Ford Model T cars were built?
hint: For scale: Volkswagen built about 21.5 million original Beetles.
card: For years it came in any colour you liked, as long as it was black.

q: In what year did Sony launch the first Walkman?
hint: For scale: the compact cassette tape was introduced in 1963.
card: Sony built the first one so a co-founder could listen to music on long flights.

q: How long was the Titanic?
hint: For scale: a football pitch is about {105 m} long.
card: Of its four funnels, only three vented smoke; the fourth was mostly for ventilation and looks.

q: How long was the Hindenburg airship?
hint: For scale: a Boeing 747 is about {70 m} long.
card: It and its sister ship remain the longest aircraft ever to fly.

q: How many spaces run around the edge of a Monopoly board?
hint: For scale: a chessboard has 64 squares.
card: The four corners are Go, Jail, Free Parking and Go to Jail.

q: How high is a basketball hoop’s rim above the floor?
hint: For scale: a typical room ceiling is about {2.4 m} high.
card: James Naismith’s first hoop, in 1891, was a peach basket nailed to a raised running track.

q: How long is a cricket pitch, from wicket to wicket?
hint: For scale: a double-decker bus is about {11 m} long.
card: The length is one chain, an old surveyor’s unit of 22 yards.

q: How many tiles come in a standard English Scrabble set, blanks included?
hint: For scale: a deck of cards has 52.
card: There’s only one Q and one Z, each worth ten points.

q: How heavy is a standard men’s Olympic weightlifting bar, without plates?
hint: For scale: a car tyre weighs about {10 kg}.
card: It is 2.2 m long; the women’s bar is a little shorter and lighter.

q: How long is a tennis court, from baseline to baseline?
hint: For scale: a basketball court is about {28 m} long.
card: The net sags in the middle, where it is about 15 cm lower than at the posts.

q: How many lines does a traditional sonnet have?
hint: For scale: a limerick has five.
card: Shakespeare wrote 154 of them.

q: How many coloured stickers cover a standard 3×3 Rubik’s Cube?
hint: For scale: a die has six faces.
card: It can be scrambled in about 43 quintillion ways, yet any position can be solved in 20 moves.

q: What is the highest score possible with three darts?
hint: For scale: the bullseye is worth 50.
card: Players call it a “ton 80”: three darts in the treble 20.

q: What is the maximum break in snooker under normal circumstances?
hint: For scale: a snooker frame starts with 15 red balls.
card: Ronnie O’Sullivan made one in just 5 minutes 8 seconds in 1997.

q: How high is the crossbar of a full-size soccer goal?
hint: For scale: a typical interior door is about {2 m} tall.
card: Goal sizes come from old British units: 8 feet high and 8 yards wide.

q: How tall is One World Trade Center in New York, including its spire?
hint: For scale: the Empire State Building’s roof is {381 m} up.
card: Its height in feet, 1,776, matches the year of the US Declaration of Independence.

q: How tall is the Atomium in Brussels?
hint: For scale: a 10-storey building is about {30 m} tall.
card: It shows a single iron crystal magnified 165 billion times.

q: How tall is the London Eye?
hint: For scale: Big Ben’s Elizabeth Tower is {96 m} tall.
card: A full turn takes about 30 minutes, slow enough that people step on and off while it keeps moving.

q: How wide is the dome of the Pantheon in Rome?
hint: For scale: a basketball court is about {28 m} long.
card: Nearly 1,900 years on, it is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world.

q: How tall is Chicago’s Willis Tower, to its roof?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is {330 m} tall with its antennas.
card: It was called the Sears Tower until 2009.

q: How tall is each letter of the Hollywood sign?
hint: For scale: a giraffe stands about {5.5 m} tall.
card: It first read “HOLLYWOODLAND” and was put up in 1923 to advertise a housing development.

q: In what year did London’s Tower Bridge open?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower was finished in 1889.
card: Its high walkways between the towers were closed in 1910 because so few people used them.

q: How tall is the Great Sphinx of Giza?
hint: For scale: a 10-storey building is about {30 m} tall.
card: It was carved from the limestone bedrock of the Giza Plateau.

q: In what year did the Channel Tunnel open?
hint: For scale: the Berlin Wall fell in 1989.
card: Its tunnels reach up to 75 m below sea level.

q: How tall is the sail-shaped Burj Al Arab hotel in Dubai?
hint: For scale: a 30-storey office tower is about {100 m} tall.
card: It stands on its own artificial island about 280 m offshore.

q: How many rooms are in Buckingham Palace?
hint: For scale: a typical family house has about six to eight rooms.
card: Queen Victoria was the first monarch to live there, from 1837.

q: How long is Hadrian’s Wall in northern England?
hint: For scale: a marathon is just over {42 km}.
card: Roman soldiers built most of it in about six years, starting around AD 122.

q: In what year was the first image of a black hole revealed?
hint: For scale: gravitational waves were first detected in 2015.
card: It showed the black hole at the centre of the galaxy M87, about 53 million light-years away.

q: Roughly how hot is the core of the Sun?
hint: For scale: the Sun’s visible surface is about {5,500 °C}.
card: Light made there can take over 100,000 years to work its way out to the surface.

q: How old is the universe?
hint: For scale: the oldest known fossils are about 3.5 billion years old.
card: Its oldest light, the afterglow of the Big Bang, was released about 380,000 years after it began.

q: How old is the Earth?
hint: For scale: the dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago.
card: The oldest known minerals on Earth, tiny zircon crystals from Australia, are about 4.4 billion years old.

q: In what year did someone first walk in space?
hint: For scale: Yuri Gagarin first flew to space in 1961.
card: Alexei Leonov’s suit ballooned so much he had to let air out to squeeze back into his spacecraft.

q: How fast does Earth travel around the Sun?
hint: For scale: a rifle bullet flies at about {1 km/s}.
card: That’s fast enough to cross the width of the United States in under three minutes.

q: How many Moons would it take to match the mass of the Earth?
hint: For scale: about 49 Moons would fit inside Earth by volume.
card: Even so, it is the fifth-largest moon in the Solar System.

q: What percentage of Earth’s gravity would you feel on the Moon?
hint: For scale: on Mars you’d feel about 38%.
card: That’s why Apollo astronauts often found it easier to hop than to walk.

q: How many constellations are officially recognised by astronomers?
hint: For scale: the zodiac has 12 constellations.
card: The largest, Hydra, sprawls across more than 3% of the whole sky.

q: In what year was Pluto discovered?
hint: For scale: Neptune was found in 1846.
card: Its name was suggested by Venetia Burney, an 11-year-old girl in Oxford.

q: How many Earth days pass between one sunrise and the next on the Moon?
hint: For scale: the Moon takes about a week to go from new to half full.
card: So a single stretch of daylight on the Moon lasts about two Earth weeks.

q: How high is the Kármán line, the most common definition of where space begins?
hint: For scale: airliners cruise about {11 km} up.
card: It is named after Theodore von Kármán, who worked out roughly where wings stop working. So is this game.

q: How many species of bear are alive today?
hint: For scale: there are seven species of sea turtle.
card: The polar bear is the largest; the sun bear of Southeast Asia is the smallest.

q: How many bones are in one human foot?
hint: For scale: the whole adult skeleton has 206.
card: Together, your two feet hold about a quarter of all the bones in your body.

q: How fast can a greyhound run?
hint: For scale: a typical town speed limit is {50 km/h}.
card: It is widely considered the fastest dog breed, with a deep chest that holds a big heart.

q: In what year did Alexander Fleming discover penicillin?
hint: For scale: the First World War ended in 1918.
card: He noticed mould killing bacteria on a dish he had left out while on holiday.

q: In what year was the double-helix structure of DNA published?
hint: For scale: the Second World War ended in 1945.
card: Rosalind Franklin’s X-ray image, “Photo 51”, was key evidence for the double helix.

q: In what year did Edward Jenner test the first vaccine, against smallpox?
hint: For scale: the US Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.
card: The word vaccine comes from vacca, Latin for cow, because he used cowpox.

q: How tall was Robert Wadlow, the tallest person ever reliably measured?
hint: For scale: a typical interior door is about {2 m} tall.
card: He was still growing when he died at the age of 22.

q: How many legs does a scorpion have?
hint: For scale: insects have six.
card: Scorpions glow blue-green under ultraviolet light.

q: How many identical babies does a nine-banded armadillo usually have in one litter?
hint: For scale: humans usually have one baby at a time.
card: All of them grow from a single fertilised egg, which is why they are identical.

q: How long can a Komodo dragon grow?
hint: For scale: a typical car is about {4.5 m} long.
card: It is the largest living lizard, and can eat up to 80% of its body weight in one meal.

q: How many toes does a typical cat have, counting all four paws?
hint: For scale: a human has 20 fingers and toes.
card: Cats with extra toes are called polydactyl; Ernest Hemingway’s house in Florida is full of them.

q: How many days does a dog’s pregnancy usually last?
hint: For scale: a human pregnancy lasts about 280 days.
card: Puppies are born with their eyes closed and open them at around ten days old.

q: In what year did the Beatles release their first single, “Love Me Do”?
hint: For scale: Elvis Presley’s first big hit, “Heartbreak Hotel”, came out in 1956.
card: A session drummer, not Ringo Starr, played on one of the released versions.

q: In what year did Disneyland open in California?
hint: For scale: the Second World War ended in 1945.
card: It was built in about a year on former orange groves in Anaheim.

q: In what year was gold found at Sutter’s Mill, starting the California Gold Rush?
hint: For scale: the Battle of Waterloo was fought in 1815.
card: San Francisco grew from about 1,000 people to around 25,000 in under two years.

q: In what year was the first Super Bowl played?
hint: For scale: the Beatles split up in 1970.
card: Officially it wasn’t the Super Bowl: it was the AFL-NFL World Championship Game.

q: In what year was Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart born?
hint: For scale: Johann Sebastian Bach died in 1750.
card: He was composing his first short pieces at the age of five.

q: In what year was the first Tour de France raced?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower was finished in 1889.
card: It was dreamed up to boost sales of a sports newspaper, L’Auto.

q: In what year was the Mona Lisa stolen from the Louvre?
hint: For scale: Paris opened its first Métro line in 1900.
card: It was missing for over two years, and the theft is a big part of why it is so famous today.

q: In what year were the first Academy Awards handed out?
hint: For scale: the first feature-length “talkie”, The Jazz Singer, came out in 1927.
card: The ceremony lasted about 15 minutes, and the winners had been announced months before.

q: How many days did the Mayflower’s voyage across the Atlantic take?
hint: For scale: a modern cruise ship crosses in about a week.
card: One baby, Oceanus Hopkins, was born on board during the crossing.

q: Roughly how many soldiers are in China’s Terracotta Army?
hint: For scale: a Roman legion had about 5,000 soldiers.
card: Each figure has its own face, and they were originally painted in bright colours.

q: For how many years did Louis XIV reign as king of France?
hint: For scale: most US presidents serve four or eight years.
card: He became king at the age of four, so his mother and ministers ruled for him at first.

q: How many children did Queen Victoria have?
hint: For scale: Henry VIII had six wives.
card: Her children married into so many royal families that she was called “the grandmother of Europe”.

q: In what year did Apple release the first Macintosh?
hint: For scale: IBM’s first PC came out in 1981.
card: It was launched with a famous TV ad inspired by George Orwell’s novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

q: In what year was the first text message sent?
hint: For scale: the first call from a handheld mobile phone was made in 1973.
card: It said “Merry Christmas” and was typed on a computer, because phones couldn’t send texts yet.

q: What was the top speed of Japan’s first bullet trains when they opened in 1964?
hint: For scale: a car on a motorway goes about {110 km/h}.
card: The line opened just days before the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

q: In what year was the QR code invented?
hint: For scale: the first barcode was scanned at a shop checkout in 1974.
card: It was designed by the Japanese firm Denso Wave to track car parts.

q: What speed did Thrust SSC reach in 1997, the first car to officially break the sound barrier?
hint: For scale: a Formula One car tops out at around {350 km/h}.
card: It was powered by two jet engines from a Phantom fighter plane.

q: How long is a Nimitz-class aircraft carrier?
hint: For scale: a football pitch is about {105 m} long.
card: Its nuclear reactors let it sail for over 20 years without refuelling.

q: How much did the Hubble Space Telescope weigh at launch?
hint: For scale: an adult African elephant weighs about {6,000 kg}.
card: It is about 13 m long, roughly the length of a big city bus.

q: In what year did the first music CDs go on sale?
hint: For scale: Pac-Man hit arcades in 1980.
card: The first album to go on sale was Billy Joel’s 52nd Street.

q: How many megabytes does a standard 3.5-inch high-density floppy disk hold?
hint: For scale: a typical phone photo is about 3 MB.
card: The “save” icon in many apps is still a picture of one.

q: How many revolutions per minute does a vinyl LP record spin at?
hint: For scale: a car engine idles at about 800 rpm.
card: LP stands for “long play”: about 23 minutes of music per side.

q: How tall was the very first Ferris wheel, built in Chicago in 1893?
hint: For scale: a 10-storey building is about {30 m} tall.
card: Each of its 36 cars could hold 60 people.

q: What top speed did Usain Bolt hit during his 2009 world-record 100 m?
hint: For scale: a brisk walk is about {5 km/h}.
card: He covered the 100 m in 9.58 seconds.

q: How high is the top platform in Olympic diving?
hint: For scale: a typical room is about {2.5 m} tall.
card: Divers have under two seconds in the air to fit in all their twists and somersaults.

q: How long is an American football field between the two goal lines?
hint: For scale: a soccer pitch is usually about {105 m} long.
card: Its painted yard lines give it the nickname “the gridiron”.

q: How far is it from the foul line to the head pin in ten-pin bowling?
hint: For scale: a double-decker bus is about {11 m} long.
card: A perfect game scores 300: twelve strikes in a row.

q: How many letters are in the Hawaiian alphabet, counting the ʻokina?
hint: For scale: English has 26.
card: They are A, E, I, O, U, H, K, L, M, N, P, W and the ʻokina, a glottal stop.

q: How long is the longer side of a sheet of A4 paper?
hint: For scale: a credit card is about 86 mm wide.
card: Fold it in half and you get A5, with exactly the same proportions.

q: How many sheets are in a standard ream of paper?
hint: For scale: a typical paperback novel has about 300 pages.
card: The word comes, via Spanish, from the Arabic rizma, meaning a bundle.

q: How many seconds does an NBA team get to take a shot?
hint: For scale: a minute has 60 seconds.
card: It arrived in 1954 to stop teams stalling; one game in 1950 had ended 19–18.

q: How many tiles are in a standard double-six set of dominoes?
hint: For scale: a deck of cards has 52.
card: Every possible pairing of 0 to 6 pips appears exactly once.

q: How heavy is a standard gold bar of the kind held by central banks?
hint: For scale: a bowling ball weighs about {7 kg}.
card: Each bar must be at least 99.5% pure gold.

q: How many squares are on a Scrabble board?
hint: For scale: a chessboard has 64.
card: Only 8 of them are triple-word squares.
